title: Killing boundary ramification in normalized Galois tensor factors
statement:
Let $R\hookrightarrow B$ be an injective map of Noetherian normal domains, with induced fraction-field inclusion $K\hookrightarrow E$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-pc-field-extension]. Fix $n\geq1$ invertible in $R$. Let $(L_j/K)_j$ be a nonempty finite family of finite Galois field extensions with $[L_j:K]\mid n$, and fix an $E$-algebra decomposition
$$\prod_j(L_j\otimes_K E)\cong\prod_a F_a$$
into a finite family of finite separable extensions $F_a/E$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], each with the structure induced by its tensor factor. Let $C_a$ be the integral closure of $B$ in $F_a$ and put $C=\prod_a C_a$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be a height-one prime (nonzero with no prime strictly between $(0)$ and $\mathfrak q$), and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$. Assume $V=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $A=B_{\mathfrak q}$ are discrete valuation rings [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], that the induced map $V\to A$ is finite and injective, and that $\mathfrak m_VA=\mathfrak m_A^{n}$. Then $C$ is a finite, hence finitely presented, $B$-algebra. For every prime $\mathfrak Q_a$ of $C_a$ over $\mathfrak q$, one has
$$\Omega_{(C_a)_{\mathfrak Q_a}/A}=0$$
[def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. For every prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $C$ over $\mathfrak q$, the local ring $C_{\mathfrak Q}$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $(\Omega_{C/B})_{\mathfrak Q}=0$, and there is $g\in C\setminus\mathfrak Q$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}C[1/g]\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is etale [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-etale-morphism]. No assumption that $B$ or $C$ is excellent is required.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed pp.133-134: codimension-one Abhyankar subargument, returned steps 11-13. proof.text: For each $a$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite] to the Noetherian normal domain $B$, its fraction field $E$, and the given finite separable extension $F_a/E$. Thus $C_a$ is finite over $B$. Choose finite module generators in every factor and insert them into the product with zero in the other coordinates; these finitely many elements generate $C$ as a $B$-module. The same elements generate it as a $B$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], $C$ is finitely presented over $B$.

Put V = R_p and A = B_q, with the localization maps into the specified fraction fields K and E. The canonical fraction field of V is V-algebra isomorphic to K. A prime kernel of the projection from the given product decomposition to F_a selects one tensor coordinate j (PrimeSpectrum.exists_comap_evalRingHom_eq). Factoring this surjective projection through coordinate evaluation gives a surjective E-algebra map L_j tensor_K E -> F_a. Its restriction iL to L_j commutes with K and its image generates F_a over E. Since A is finite faithful over V, E is also the localization of A at the nonzero elements of V. The inverses of these elements lie in iL(L_j), so the same image generates F_a as an A-algebra. Tensor lifting therefore gives a surjection L_j tensor_V A -> F_a, identifying F_a with the quotient by a maximal ideal and respecting its specified A-structure. The private helpers tensor_field_factor and adjoin_over_finite_dvr_extension implement these comparisons.

source.place: Tag 0BRM (lemma-abhyankar), generic tensor-product setup; explicit finite-dimensional linear-algebra and localization argument for the input of lem-sbc-dvr-tame-tensor-factor-unramified.

proof.text:
Put $T=B\setminus\mathfrak q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization],
$$S_a=T^{-1}C_a=\overline A^{\,F_a},$$
as subrings of $F_a$: localizing the field $F_a$ at the nonzero images of $T$ leaves that field unchanged. Localizing the finite module generators from Step 1 makes $S_a$ finite over $A$. A prime $\mathfrak Q_a$ over $\mathfrak q$ is disjoint from $T$, hence gives $Q'_a=T^{-1}\mathfrak Q_a$ in $S_a$, contracting to $\mathfrak m_A$. The fractions in $(S_a)_{Q'_a}$ and $(C_a)_{\mathfrak Q_a}$ have precisely the same denominators after iterated localization, so these rings are canonically equal as $A$-algebras.

source.place: Tag 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize); localization at the chosen boundary prime.

proof.text: For the selected j, apply [lem-sbc-dvr-galois-normalization-ramification-dvd] over V to L_j after transporting its K-algebra structure along Frac(V) ≃ K. The Galois property, finrank, and divisibility by n transport along this equivalence. Apply [lem-sbc-dvr-tame-tensor-factor-unramified] to the maximal tensor quotient constructed in Step 2, using the finite normalization S_a and its closed prime from Step 3. This gives formal unramifiedness of (S_a)_Q over A. The private helper tame_compositum_unramified_same makes this application and transports through the quotient and integral-closure equivalences. To accommodate the upstream lemmas' single universe without restricting the item's independent universes, tame_compositum_unramified uses Module.Finite.small to replace A and L_j by Shrink models in V's universe. DVR, Galois, finite normalization, ideal-power, and finrank data transport along the ring and algebra equivalences. Localized normalization and formally unramified maps transport back. Step 3 then gives vanishing of the relative Kahler differentials for (C_a)_{Q_a}.

source.place: Tags 09EB (lemma-galois-conclusion) and 0BRM (lemma-abhyankar), in the existing two DVR lemmas; formal unramifiedness is their stated vanishing of differentials.

proof.text: The localization $(C_a)_{\mathfrak Q_a}$ embeds in $F_a$, since $C_a$ is a subring of that field and every element inverted is nonzero. Also $A\hookrightarrow F_a$ is injective. Thus, if $0\ne b\in A$ and $bx=0$ in this local ring, the same equation in $F_a$ gives $x=0$. It is torsion-free over $A$. A DVR is a principal ideal domain by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], so [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] gives flatness over $A$.

source.place: Tag 0AUW (lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat), part (1), applied to the torsion-free localized subring of a field.

proof.text: A prime of the finite product C selects one factor, using PrimeSpectrum.exists_comap_evalRingHom_eq. The bijective map Localization.AtPrime.mapPiEvalRingHom identifies C_Q with the corresponding (C_a)_{Q_a}. Its compatibility with the canonical A-localization maps transfers flatness from Step 5 and formal unramifiedness from Step 4. Formal unramifiedness of B -> A, which is a localization, and composition give formal unramifiedness of B -> C_Q. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] the canonical map Omega(C/B) -> Omega(C_Q/B) is a localization of modules. Since the latter is zero, so is (Omega(C/B))_Q. These steps are implemented by the proved private helper pi_boundary_local_properties and the canonical localized-module isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00RT (lemma-differentials-localize), parts (1) and (2); finite-product localization written explicitly using coordinate idempotents.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-etale-at-prime-flat-unramified-criterion] to $B\to C$ and $\mathfrak Q$. Finite presentation is Step 1, its contracted prime is $\mathfrak q$, and its flatness and localized differential-vanishing hypotheses are Step 6. The criterion supplies $g\in C\setminus\mathfrak Q$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}C[1/g]\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is etale. This proves all assertions. The finiteness input was the separable-extension theorem over a Noetherian normal domain, which has no excellence hypothesis.
